claims.text: Designing a specific phase distribution in a eutectic high-entropy alloy will simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
Controlled heat treatment followed by quenching can produce a refined microstructure with a balanced phase distribution.
Quenching will retain the desired phase distribution produced at the phase-transformation temperature.
The refined phase distribution promotes dislocation movement.
The refined phase distribution promotes phase stability.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and phase interactions improve strength.
Solid-solution strengthening is responsible for the proposed strength improvement.
Phase-toughening mechanisms are responsible for the proposed ductility improvement.
The heat-treated alloy will have approximately 10–20% greater yield strength than the conventional-microstructure baseline.
The heat-treated alloy will have approximately 5–15% greater ductility than the conventional-microstructure baseline.
The proposed improvements depend on controlled heat treatment and quenching and may not extend to other processing methods or extreme temperatures.
The magnitudes of the strength and ductility improvements may vary with alloy composition and heat-treatment parameters.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation between the heat-treated alloy and a baseline alloy.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% yield-strength increase and a 5% ductility increase is specified as the falsification criterion.
